candidate.smallest_test: Decompose the already isolated mod-286 interaction and replay top conjugate Fourier mode groups on the 196 existing post-discovery rows.

decision: The finite interaction has no tiny-character explanation.  The zero Fourier axes are numerically absent, confirming that the previous ANOVA interaction split is respected, but the top two, four, six, and eight conjugacy groups do not both explain the sign and magnitude.  The first sign-stable truncation uses 10 conjugacy groups, but its minimum contribution-to-total ratio is only 0.009071759166255295. The first tested truncation carrying at least half the drag on every row uses 20 conjugacy groups.  The surviving theorem target is a band-limited signed interaction inequality plus a residual bound, or a direct raw q286-WBSS signed-witness estimate.
status_boundary: finite mod-286 Fourier-interaction diagnostic only; no multiplicative-character theorem, signed projection theorem, q286 threshold theorem, strict-central Goldbach theorem, or Goldbach proof
